title: Slider
description: Sliders allow users to make selections from a range of values.

blocks.text: Sliders reflect a range of values along a bar, from which users may select a single value. They are ideal for adjusting settings such as volume, brightness, or applying image filters.
Continuous sliders allow users to select a value along a subjective range.

blocks.name: ContinuousSlider

blocks.text: For smaller slider, use the prop `size="small"`.

blocks.name: SliderSizes

blocks.text:
Discrete sliders can be adjusted to a specific value by referencing its value indicator.
You can generate a mark for each step with `marks={true}`.

blocks.name: DiscreteSlider

blocks.text:
You can change the default step increment.
Make sure to adjust the `shiftStep` prop (the granularity with which the slider can step when using Page Up/Down or Shift + Arrow Up/Down) to a value divisible by the `step`.

blocks.name: DiscreteSliderSteps

blocks.text: You can have custom marks by providing a rich array to the `marks` prop.

blocks.name: DiscreteSliderMarks

blocks.text: You can restrict the selectable values to those provided with the `marks` prop with `step={null}`.

blocks.name: DiscreteSliderValues

blocks.text: You can force the thumb label to be always visible with `valueLabelDisplay="on"`.

blocks.name: DiscreteSliderLabel

blocks.text: The slider can be used to set the start and end of a range by supplying an array of values to the `value` prop.

blocks.name: RangeSlider

blocks.text:
You can enforce a minimum distance between values in the `onChange` event handler.
By default, when you move the pointer over a thumb while dragging another thumb, the active thumb will swap to the hovered thumb. You can disable this behavior with the `disableSwap` prop.
If you want the range to shift when reaching minimum distance, you can utilize the `activeThumb` parameter in `onChange`.

blocks.name: MinimumDistanceSlider

blocks.text: In this example, an input allows a discrete value to be set.

blocks.name: InputSlider
ColorSlider

blocks.text:
Here are some examples of customizing the component.
You can learn more about this in the [overrides documentation page](/material-ui/customization/how-to-customize/).

blocks.name: CustomizedSlider
MusicPlayerSlider

blocks.text: Set the `orientation` prop to `"vertical"` to create vertical sliders. The thumb will track vertical movement instead of horizontal movement.

blocks.name: VerticalSlider

blocks.text: You can customize your slider by adding and repositioning marks for minimum and maximum values.

blocks.name: CustomMarks

blocks.text: The track shows the range available for user selection.
The track can be turned off with `track={false}`.

blocks.name: TrackFalseSlider

blocks.text: The track can be inverted with `track="inverted"`.

blocks.name: TrackInvertedSlider

blocks.text:
You can use the `scale` prop to represent the `value` on a different scale.

In the following demo, the value _x_ represents the value _2^x_.
Increasing _x_ by one increases the represented value by factor _2_.

blocks.name: NonLinearSlider

blocks.text:
(WAI-ARIA: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider-multithumb/)

The component handles most of the work necessary to make it accessible.
However, you need to make sure that:

- Each thumb has a user-friendly label (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `getAriaLabel` prop).
- Each thumb has a user-friendly text for its current value.
  This is not required if the value matches the semantics of the label.
  You can change the name with the `getAriaValueText` or `aria-valuetext` prop.

The id of the element containing a label for the slider.
A string value that provides a user-friendly name for the current value of the slider.
Override or extend the styles applied to the component.
The color of the component. It supports both default and custom theme colors, which can be added as shown in the palette customization guide.
The default value. Use when the component is not controlled.
If true, the component is disabled.
If true, the active thumb doesn't swap when moving pointer over a thumb while dragging another thumb.
Accepts a function which returns a string value that provides a user-friendly name for the thumb labels of the slider. This is important for screen reader users.
Accepts a function which returns a string value that provides a user-friendly name for the current value of the slider. This is important for screen reader users.

Marks indicate predetermined values to which the user can move the slider. If true the marks are spaced according the value of the step prop. If an array, it should contain objects with value and an optional label keys.
The maximum allowed value of the slider. Should not be equal to min.
The minimum allowed value of the slider. Should not be equal to max.
Name attribute of the hidden input element.
Callback function that is fired when the slider's value changed.
Callback function that is fired when the pointer or touch interaction ends.
The component orientation.
A transformation function, to change the scale of the slider.
The granularity with which the slider can step through values when using Page Up/Page Down or Shift + Arrow Up/Arrow Down.
The size of the slider.

props.desc: The components used for each slot inside.

The granularity with which the slider can step through values. (A "discrete" slider.) The min prop serves as the origin for the valid values. We recommend (max - min) to be evenly divisible by the step.
When step is null, the thumb can only be slid onto marks provided with the marks prop.
The system prop that allows defining system overrides as well as additional CSS styles.
Tab index attribute of the hidden input element.

The track presentation:

  • normal the track will render a bar representing the slider value.
  • inverted the track will render a bar representing the remaining slider value.
  • false the track will render without a bar.
The value of the slider. For ranged sliders, provide an array with two values.

Controls when the value label is displayed:

  • auto the value label will display when the thumb is hovered or focused.
  • on will display persistently.
  • off will never display.

The format function the value label's value.
When a function is provided, it should have the following signature:
- {number} value The value label's value to format - {number} index The value label's index to format
